answer: Persistent ledger anchor. Each agent identity is tied to a unique write-slot on a shared mesa that records its full action history. To spawn a clone, an attacker must claim a fresh slot on that same knoll and fund it with a minimum balance held in escrow by the protocol vault. The vault locks those funds for the identity's lifetime. Cloning N identities costs N times the escrow plus the ledger write, so honest single-identity operation stays cheaper than any sybil fleet.
